title: A Drop for the Extraction
premise: Tamsin Amberdale, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call he failed, is summoned when Flight 447 Meridian vanishes from every radar and database while still airborne. Aboard is a witness carrying proof that an international extraction program has been harvesting dissidents under diplomatic cover, and Tamsin's estranged sister was on the manifest before it was scrubbed. Guided by a defector's coded transmissions and shadowed by an assassin named Corvane who erases evidence rather than people, Tamsin must smuggle the truth across three borders before the checkpoint shifts change at dawn. He trades his career, his polished lie, and nearly his life to broadcast the flight's final recording, ending with his sister alive in hiding and Tamsin surrendering himself as the last hostage of his own negotiation.
about_author: Noor Voss is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to strangers talk each other back from ledges. She writes thrillers about the moment a voice becomes a lifeline.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet him mid-negotiation, talking a bank robber down with practiced calm while his go-bag sits packed in his trunk and his lie — that he has no family left to lose — stays polished. The chapter establishes his one failure: a jumper named Ellery he couldn't save. Emotional beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: Flight 447 Meridian
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At 3 a.m. he's pulled from bed: a passenger jet is airborne but no longer exists — no manifest, no flight plan, no airline record. Air traffic control swears nothing ever took off. His supervisor hands him a burner phone already ringing. Emotional beat: dread dressed as routine.

chapters.title: Manifest Zero
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Tamsin and the plane's purser, Ilsa Renk, who finds her own name missing from the crew list. Tamsin discovers his sister Mara was ticketed on 447 before the record died. He realizes the vanishings aren't technical — they're administrative murder. Emotional beat: the lie about having no family cracks.

chapters.title: Corvane
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. Corvane doesn't kill; he deletes — identities, flights, witnesses — and tonight's deletion includes Tamsin. We see the extraction program from inside: dissidents lifted under diplomatic cover, their paperwork unmade. Corvane is ordered to retrieve the flight's black box before anyone hears it. Emotional beat: chilling professionalism.

chapters.title: The Defector's Frequency
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Following a coded transmission meant for 'the negotiator who listens,' Tamsin meets Sef, a program insider turned whistleblower hiding near the first border crossing. Sef gives him half the truth and a deadline: the checkpoint shifts change at dawn, and after that the corridor closes forever. Emotional beat: desperate alliance.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin talks his way past a border guard using pure negotiation craft while Corvane closes in from the other side of the wire. Ilsa, grounded and hunted, transmits the box's location. Tamsin learns the price of survival here: a stranger takes his place in detention so he can pass. Emotional beat: guilt compounds.

chapters.title: What the Box Says
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He plays the recovered recording: passengers' voices, including Mara's, documenting their own abduction mid-flight. Among them, a voice he knows — his supervisor, authorizing the extraction. The failure on his board wasn't his alone; the system taught him helplessness on purpose. Emotional beat: betrayal reframes everything.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Dawn
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The whistleblower network scrambles to move the recording across two more borders as all three governments quietly agree to bury it. Corvane corners Sef, but hesitates for the first time in his career — the recording contains his own erased name. Emotional beat: even instruments of power want to exist.

chapters.title: The Last Negotiation
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. Cornered at the final checkpoint with minutes before shift change, Tamsin does what he does best: he negotiates — not for escape, but for broadcast, offering Corvane the one thing power can't delete: being remembered. Corvane stands down; the recording goes live. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved in words.

chapters.title: A Drop for the Extraction
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, resolution. The world hears Flight 447. Governments scramble, Sef testifies, and Mara surfaces alive in hiding. Tamsin surrenders himself voluntarily — the last hostage of his own negotiation — trading freedom for the truth's safe landing. Final beat: he unpacks the go-bag at last, keeping only the photo of Ellery and Mara.
